correctness.rationale: The initial deletion-prefix phase is congruent to the first kept letter. Because no further deleted letter can match any of the next q-1 source symbols, a full cyclic rotation is forced. This repeats after every kept q-block. Deletion counts before/between blocks have least nonnegative residues, yielding necessity of E_q(s)<=qk. The explicit deletion/retention construction using exactly the minimum phase increments, then deleting any residual suffix, proves sufficiency. Unique first letters of rotations and a bijection between phase sequences and bounded digits prove exact counting. Maximizing the digit sum gives sharp threshold; standard iid CLT gives the stated fixed-q limit. Boundary m=0,k=0 covered. Exact residual sets matched positional masks for 56 cases; an independent DP and coefficient convolution matched for 112 cases. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The precise observation is the inverse-shuffle/deletion complement of a prescribed repeated period, a canonical family motivated by the newly defined complement scattered-factor operator. The all-parameter q-ary phase language determines every survivor set and its exact size, a sharp full-support threshold, and its probabilistic transition. The joint q>=3,k>=2 regime was not obtained by merely substituting alphabet size into the known binary argument; it requires a structural forced-block lemma applicable to all cycles. No arbitrary numerical cutoff or isolated unmotivated case is used; remaining limitations are explicit.
